summary: Source-checked partial survey of Exchangeability, concentrating on its boundary with DenseGraphLimits. Both complete upstream documents were read. Two narrowly scoped overlaps are recorded: the generic exchangeable relational-law adapter, and finite sampling with versus without replacement. No new prerequisite edge is justified by this checkpoint. In particular, graphon-mixture existence does not acquire an Aldous-Hoover dependency. Three additional nearby roadmap documents were examined to the explicitly stated depth. The full catalogue and all existing-link packets have not been exhausted; none means no relationship established in the recorded read scope, not proof of absence.

overlaps.detail: Exchangeability Layer 8 owns the general exchangeable-array representation programme. DenseGraphLimits Layer 9b explicitly assigns generic consistent relational laws, relabeling invariance, dissociation and extremality outside its graph-specialized development, naming Exchangeability as the natural owner. The overlap is in this law-level interface, not in the proofs of the two representation theorems. DenseGraphLimits expressly makes its graphLawArrayLawEquiv an interface obligation rather than a build dependency, and proves graphon-mixture existence by empirical mixing, collisions and graphon compactness.
overlaps.proposal: Keep both roadmaps and their independent representation proofs. Exchangeability should specify the generic law API for the one-sort symmetric irreflexive Boolean binary signature, including finite restriction and joint relabeling. DenseGraphLimits retains the graph-specialized structures and owns the measurable graphCoordEquiv/graphLawArrayLawEquiv adapters, using unordered non-diagonal edge coordinates. Require a commuting relabeling square and preservation of finite marginals and dissociation. Prove compatibility of the graph specialization of the generic representation with the graphon-mixture law: equality is of infinite graph laws and of mixing measures on GraphonSpaceI, never of raw graphon representatives. Do not add an Aldous-Hoover-to-graphon-mixture prerequisite edge, and do not substitute the sequence iid/extreme-point theorem for the array theorem. The generic law-level declarations remain to be specified more finely within the existing Layer 8 scope.

overlaps.detail: Exchangeability Layer 8 develops random finite populations sampled through unrestricted versus injective index maps and a choose(m,2)/n eventwise error. DenseGraphLimits Layer 9a asks for the homomorphism-versus-injective-density bound with the same collision constant. The common proof is the comparison of uniform maps with uniform injections, not the full finite de Finetti theorem and not an equality of empirical graphon mixing with empirical iid laws. The current texts do not assign this reusable elementary comparison to a single owner.
overlaps.proposal: Home the general finite-population sampling/comparison API with Exchangeability Layer 8 in a neutral probability namespace. For finite kappa of cardinality n>0 and finite iota of cardinality m<=n, compare the uniform law on iota->kappa with its conditioning on injectivity; bound the collision probability by choose(m,2)/n. Export the expectation bound for measurable tests valued in [0,1], including mixtures over a probability law of populations. DenseGraphLimits retains homDensityFin, injHomDensity, their graph-specific pushforward/test identifications, the unbiasedness theorem, and the joint graphon sampler. Its graph-density estimate is the deterministic-population/Boolean-test specialization, with the ordered-injection denominator (n)_m, not choose(n,m). Treat m=0 and n=1 explicitly and leave n=0 outside the division theorem. Do not add a directed stage link until the common comparison and graph-test adapter are specified; do not make graph sampling wait for the exchangeable-array representation summit.
